faqs.q: What should I check first when my Mercury outboard will not start?
faqs.a: Confirm the control is firmly in neutral, the emergency-stop lanyard is clipped in, the battery switch and connections are sound, and fuel can reach the engine. Note whether the starter does nothing, clicks, cranks slowly or cranks normally, because each points to a different diagnostic path.

faqs.q: How often should a Mercury outboard be serviced?
faqs.a: For many recreational Mercury FourStroke engines, annual or every 100 hours is the main service interval, whichever comes first. Some items are due around 300 hours or three years. The schedule in the serial-specific owner manual overrides any general rule.

faqs.q: Can I maintain my Mercury outboard myself without voiding the warranty?
faqs.a: Mercury allows owner maintenance, but you must follow the correct manual, use suitable parts and fluids, and keep records. Damage caused by incorrect service is not covered. Warranty claims are handled through an authorized Mercury dealer.

faqs.q: What does a beeping Mercury outboard mean?
faqs.a: It means the engine or connected system has detected a condition that needs attention, but there is no single universal beep decoder for every model and year. Record the exact tone, display icon or message, rpm and operating conditions, then consult the correct manual or arrange diagnostics.

faqs.q: Is 10W-30 or 25W-40 correct for my Mercury outboard?
faqs.a: Both are correct for different Mercury families. The 2026 capacity guide lists 10W-30 for many 2.5-30 HP and current V6/V8 families, while 25W-40 appears on 40-60 HP, legacy 1.7 L 75/90/115 and several Verado families. Use the exact model and serial-number manual.

articles.title: Mercury Command Thrust: The Real Talk Guide (BigFoot History, Pontoons vs V-Hulls)

faqs.q: Is Command Thrust the same thing as BigFoot?
faqs.a: Yes. BigFoot was the 1990s name for Mercury's big-gearcase pontoon and workboat option. Mercury renamed it Command Thrust around 2014. Same concept: bigger gearcase, taller gear ratio, bigger prop, more push power at low speed.

faqs.q: Does Command Thrust make the same horsepower?
faqs.a: Yes. A 60 CT and a standard 60 have identical powerheads. CT changes the gearcase, gear ratio, and prop, which changes how the power reaches the water, not how much power there is.

faqs.q: Should I get Command Thrust on my pontoon?
faqs.a: Almost certainly yes if you're 90 HP and up on a 20+ ft pontoon, and it's worth a conversation on smaller setups. CT is the standard pontoon choice at HBW. See the pontoon eligibility guide for size-by-size calls.

faqs.q: Should I get Command Thrust on my fishing boat?
faqs.a: Almost certainly no. On a planing aluminum or fibreglass V-hull, CT adds drag and costs top speed with no meaningful benefit. Standard gearcase with the right prop is the better setup. The exception is workboat duty or a ProKicker for trolling.

articles.description: What affects milky gearcase oil repair cost in Ontario, what can cause water intrusion, how a technician tests the gearcase, and what to do next.

faqs.q: What does milky gearcase oil mean?
faqs.a: Water has gotten into your lower unit and emulsified with the gear oil, almost always past a worn prop shaft, driveshaft, or shift shaft seal. It needs a pressure test to locate the leak and a reseal, and the earlier it's caught, the cheaper it stays.

faqs.q: Can I just change the oil and keep boating?
faqs.a: No. Refilling does not identify or repair the source of water intrusion. Mercury warns that water-contaminated lubricant can damage bearings and can freeze inside the gearcase. Have the gearcase inspected before further operation.

faqs.q: How much does a gearcase pressure test cost?
faqs.a: The test pressurizes and vacuum-checks the case to identify which seal leaks; it's quoted work, confirmed when you book. It's the step that turns 'there's water in it somewhere' into a precise, priced repair instead of a guess. Start at hbw.wiki/service.

faqs.q: What causes gearcase seals to fail?
faqs.a: Fishing line wrapped behind the prop is the classic killer; age, impact, and corrosion do the rest. Pulling the prop periodically to check for line is the cheapest prevention there is, and it's part of every annual service.

faqs.q: Is the Mercury 9.9 ProKicker better than a regular 9.9 for trolling?

faqs.q: Can I run an electric trolling motor on Rice Lake?
faqs.a: Yes, and many anglers do, especially in the shallow bays and weed flats. Battery range becomes a factor on Rice Lake open water. A lithium battery upgrade substantially extends range if you plan to fish the whole lake.

faqs.q: What size trolling motor do I need for my fishing boat?
faqs.a: General starting point: 2 lbs of thrust per 100 lbs of loaded boat weight, then round up. A 1,800 lb loaded aluminum boat needs roughly 36 lbs of thrust minimum. Most anglers opt for 25 to 36 kg (55 to 80 lb) units to handle wind.

articles.description: Cold-water boating safety for Ontario waters. Risks, essential gear, weather awareness, and emergency procedures for spring, fall.

faqs.q: When should I stop boating in Ontario for the season?
faqs.a: Most Ontario boaters wrap up by late October or early November. Key factors: water temperature below 10°C, ice forming on shorelines, and inability to dress appropriately for conditions. Safety margins shrink dramatically in cold water.

faqs.q: What water temperature is dangerous for immersion?
faqs.a: Any water below 21°C (70°F) can cause hypothermia. Below 15°C is dangerous within 30-40 minutes. Below 10°C is immediately dangerous. Ontario fall waters typically range from 10-18°C.

faqs.q: What's the most important safety gear for fall boating?
faqs.a: A worn PFD - not just carried. In cold water, you have seconds to minutes before losing the ability to swim. A float coat combines warmth and flotation, making it ideal for fall conditions.

faqs.q: Should I always wear a PFD in fall?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Cold water shock can incapacitate you in seconds. You may not have time to put on a PFD if you fall in. Transport Canada recommends wearing PFDs whenever on the water, especially in cold conditions.

faqs.q: Is fall service cheaper than spring service?

faqs.q: Why is my Mercury overheating only at idle?
faqs.a: Almost always a partially-blocked or worn water pump impeller. At cruise RPM, enough water gets through to keep temps OK; at idle, there isn't enough flow. Standard fix is impeller replacement (1-2 hour service job).

faqs.q: How often should I replace the impeller?
faqs.a: Every 3 years or 300 hours, whichever comes first (Mercury official interval). Mercury recommends inspection annually. If you boat in weedy water (like Rice Lake), lean toward 2 years.

faqs.q: My tell-tale is weak, can I still run it?
faqs.a: Briefly at idle to limp back to dock, yes. Anything more risks the powerhead. The tell-tale stream is your real-time water-flow indicator - if it's weak, the engine is undercooled.

faqs.q: Can I just delete the thermostat to fix overheating?
faqs.a: No. Engines need to reach operating temp to combust properly. A deleted thermostat means lifelong rich-running, fouled plugs, worse fuel economy, more emissions. Fix the actual problem.

faqs.q: Can a pontoon handle Lake Ontario?
faqs.a: On a calm summer day, yes, a modern tritoon with the right power can handle Lake Ontario near shore. On a typical windy afternoon, no, the chop will be uncomfortable at best and dangerous at worst. For consistent Lake Ontario use, V-hull is the right call.

faqs.q: What's the fastest pontoon a 90 HP Mercury can push?
faqs.a: A 90 ELPT with Command Thrust on a 20-foot pontoon will hit 25-28 mph (40-45 km/h) on a calm day with light load. A 22-foot tritoon with the same motor lands closer to 22-25 mph (35-40 km/h). Going faster requires more horsepower (115-150 HP) and usually a tritoon configuration.

faqs.q: Are pontoons safe in waves?
faqs.a: Pontoons are stable but not seaworthy in the same sense as V-hulls. They handle small chop fine (under 1 foot) but get bounced around in 2-foot waves and can take water over the front deck in larger conditions. Stay on calmer water and watch the wind forecast.

faqs.q: Can I trailer a pontoon as easily as a V-hull?
faqs.a: Pontoons require a wider trailer and a special bunk arrangement. Towing is similar in weight (often lighter than a comparable fiberglass V-hull) but the width and wind load make highway driving less forgiving. Most pontoon owners keep the boat at a slip rather than trailer regularly.

faqs.q: Are aluminum hulls noisier than fiberglass?
faqs.a: Yes, marginally. Aluminum transmits more wake-slap and rivet noise. Modern welded hulls with foam-injection are quieter than older riveted designs. Most owners stop noticing within a season.

faqs.q: Does aluminum corrode in fresh water?
faqs.a: Marine-grade aluminum (5052 or 5086 alloy) resists fresh-water corrosion well for decades. The exception is galvanic corrosion at fittings where dissimilar metals contact aluminum without proper isolation. A boat kept in the water year-round needs sacrificial zincs and proper fitting installation. A trailered boat tha…

faqs.q: Can fiberglass survive Ontario winters in outdoor storage?
faqs.a: Yes, with proper preparation. Drain all water, cover with shrinkwrap or a quality cover, keep the cockpit drains clear so meltwater drains out. Cracked gelcoat and water intrusion from a winter of standing water is the most common avoidable fiberglass damage we see.

faqs.q: Are aluminum boats colder to fish from in shoulder seasons?
faqs.a: Aluminum decks transmit cold more than fiberglass decks. A carpeted aluminum boat is a non-issue; a bare-aluminum-deck boat in October is genuinely cold. Most modern aluminum fishing boats have carpet or rubber matting that solves this.

faqs.q: What happens if the DTS digital display fails on the water?

faqs.q: Are mechanical cables really 50-year-old technology?
faqs.a: Functionally, yes. Modern cables have better materials and seals, but the principle has not changed. They wear out predictably (most cables are good for 10-15 years of average use), they're cheap, and they're easy to replace.

faqs.q: My motor sat unused for two seasons. Do I need anything beyond this checklist?
faqs.a: Probably yes. Two-year storage usually means stale fuel (definitely drain), possibly damaged fuel lines, and a higher chance of impeller failure. A full pre-launch service is worth the few hundred dollars. We've seen multiple cases where the owner skipped this and the first start did $3,000-$5,000 of damage.

faqs.q: Is it ok to run my Mercury on a hose with earmuffs for the first start?
faqs.a: Yes, with a properly-fitted flush attachment that delivers enough water flow. This is how dealers do first-starts for new motors. It's also how careful owners verify the cooling system before the boat goes in the water. Just confirm strong water flow at the muffs and the telltale before running.

faqs.q: My battery reads 11.8 volts. Can I jump-start it and go boating?
faqs.a: You can, but you shouldn't expect the battery to recover under boat use. Jumping a deeply-discharged battery to start the motor is a one-way trip: the alternator output isn't enough to fully recharge a deeply-discharged marine battery under typical use. Replace the battery, then go boating.

faqs.q: Does ethanol-free premium fuel solve all my fuel problems?
faqs.a: No, but it helps. Ethanol-free fuel doesn't phase-separate in storage and doesn't attract water. It's worth the extra cost if available, especially for boats that get used infrequently or stored for long periods. Stabil or Sta-Bil 360 also helps for any fuel.

faqs.q: Can I keep running if a Mercury warning stops after a restart?
faqs.a: Don’t use a restart as proof the cause is gone. Record the warning and follow the owner’s manual. If it returns, performance changes or the manual requires shutdown, stop operating.

faqs.q: Does a strong telltale mean the engine cannot be overheating?
faqs.a: No. The telltale is one observation, not a complete temperature diagnosis. It can’t rule out an overheating problem. Treat a temperature warning according to the exact engine manual.

faqs.q: Can a slightly damaged propeller wait until winter?
faqs.a: A new vibration or impact deserves prompt inspection. Visible damage may not show every affected component, and continued operation can add wear.

faqs.q: Is 12.6 volts enough to prove a battery is healthy?
faqs.a: No. Resting voltage does not prove cranking capacity. A questionable, fully charged battery should be load-tested, and the connections and charging system also matter.

faqs.a: Usually you don't recover the full cost. faqs.q: Is it safe to add a trolling motor or fishfinder myself?
faqs.a: Yes, if you use marine-grade wire, marine-grade terminals, and a properly-sized fuse on the positive lead at the battery. The wrong installation is a fire risk and an electrical-fault generator. If you're not sure, have a marine electrician do it.

faqs.q: My bilge pump runs every few minutes even when the boat is dry. What's wrong?
faqs.a: Usually a stuck float switch or a leaking through-hull fitting that's letting water in. Inspect both. A pump that cycles constantly will wear out fast and drain the battery.

faqs.q: Can I use household electrical tape for marine connections?
faqs.a: Not as a permanent solution. Electrical tape degrades from UV, humidity, and heat. For permanent connections use adhesive-lined heat-shrink. Tape is fine for a one-trip emergency fix only.

faqs.q: Why does my electrical system seem fine in summer but fail in spring?
faqs.a: Winter storage creates the perfect conditions for corrosion: temperature swings cause condensation cycles, the boat sits dormant so any moisture trapped in connections can't dry, and rodents sometimes chew through wiring undetected. Spring is when the accumulated damage shows up.

faqs.q: Is FourStroke better than Pro XS?
faqs.a: Neither is "better", they're tuned for different use cases. FourStroke prioritizes fuel efficiency, quiet operation, and longevity. Pro XS prioritizes acceleration, top-end speed, and tournament-grade performance. For most Ontario freshwater boating, FourStroke is the right tool.

faqs.q: How long does a Mercury FourStroke last?
faqs.a: Properly maintained, 15-25 years of useful service is realistic. The motor that fails early is almost always one that missed oil changes, skipped impeller replacements, or got winterized improperly. Brand matters less than service habits.

faqs.q: Is a FourStroke heavier than the 2-stroke it replaces?
faqs.a: Yes. A 90 HP FourStroke weighs roughly 163 kg, about 163 kg (359 lb), compared to about 140 to 145 kg for an older 90 HP 2-stroke. The 15 to 25 kg of added weight matters for transom strength and boat trim.

faqs.q: Will my boat still perform well with a FourStroke?

faqs.q: What is a poppet valve and why does it matter at high RPM?
faqs.a: The poppet valve is a pressure-relief valve in the cooling system that opens at higher RPM to increase water flow through the powerhead. If it's clogged or weak, it can't open properly, and the motor overheats only at speed. It's the most commonly missed cause of a high-RPM-only overheat.

faqs.q: I replaced the impeller and it still overheats at speed. Now what?
faqs.a: Check the poppet valve and the intake screens. A fresh impeller can't fix a stuck poppet or a partial flow restriction. This is a very common sequence, and it's usually why the impeller swap didn't solve it.

faqs.q: How long can I run my Mercury while it's overheating?
faqs.a: Don't. Even a few minutes at temperature can warp components or cook the powerhead. Throttle back to idle the moment the alarm sounds, confirm you have water flow, and limp in. A repair is a fraction of the cost of a new powerhead.

faqs.q: Why didn't my bilge pump turn on when there was water in the boat?
faqs.a: The most common cause is a float switch that's stuck, worn out, or no longer getting power through a corroded connector. The pump motor itself is usually fine. Test the manual override at the helm first. If it runs, the motor is good and the problem is in the float switch circuit.

faqs.q: What's the difference between the manual and automatic bilge pump switch?
faqs.a: Manual runs the pump on demand from the helm, useful for testing or clearing water you can see. Automatic relies on the float switch to trigger the pump on its own, which is what protects the boat when you're not on board.

faqs.q: Can I test my float switch without hauling the boat?
faqs.a: Yes. With the helm switch set to auto, gently lift the float arm by hand to where rising water would push it. The pump should start within a second or two. If it doesn't, the problem is in the switch circuit.

faqs.q: Is it safe to run my bilge pump dry to see if it works?
faqs.a: No. Bilge pumps are built to move water, and running one dry can damage the impeller or motor within seconds. Test with the float arm and a small amount of water, not a dry run.

articles.description: A detailed comparison of Mercury 90 hp and 115 hp FourStroke outboards for Ontario aluminum boats, covering weight, performance, fuel economy, price, and resale value.

faqs.q: Can I put a 115 hp engine on a boat rated for 90 hp?
faqs.a: Treat 90 HP as the manufacturer's maximum recommended safe power unless authoritative documentation for the exact hull says otherwise. Do not use an oversized existing setup as approval. A 115 HP setup can create serious safety, insurance, warranty, liability, financing, and resale problems.

faqs.q: Is the Mercury 115 FourStroke just a tuned 90?
faqs.a: Essentially, yes. The 90 hp and 115 hp FourStroke share the same 2.1L block and many internal components. Differences in ECM tuning, camshaft design, and throttle-body size allow the 115 to deliver more power, but the core engine is nearly identical in weight and dimensions.

faqs.q: How much fuel will I save by choosing the 90 hp over the 115?
faqs.a: At typical cruising speeds the difference is minor, often within half a litre per hour. Both motors are efficient four-strokes. The 115 may use slightly more fuel at wide-open throttle, but its ability to plane at lower RPM with heavy loads can offset that in real-world use.

faqs.q: Do both engines come with Command Thrust?
faqs.a: Yes. Both the Mercury 90 hp and 115 hp FourStroke are available with the Command Thrust gearcase option. If you often carry heavy loads, pull watersports gear, or operate at higher elevations, the CT gearcase is worth considering on either engine.

faqs.q: How long is the break-in period on a new Mercury outboard?
faqs.a: Break-in length depends on the engine family. The schedule, duration, and RPM limits vary by engine family and model year, so check the owner's manual for your serial number for the exact routine. Read our break-in guide for the plain-language version.

faqs.q: When should I do the first oil change on my Mercury outboard?
faqs.a: Mercury's published maintenance schedule calls for oil and filter service at 100 hours or annually, whichever comes first. Many owners and dealers like an early change around 20 hours to flush break-in debris; that's a common best practice, not a Mercury requirement.

faqs.q: Do I need to use the Mercury Marine app with my new outboard?
faqs.a: It's not required for basic operation, but pairing the Mercury Marine app via SmartCraft Connect gives you engine hours, fault codes, maintenance reminders, and digital gauges on your phone. Worth doing in the first week.

faqs.q: What does a beep from my Mercury outboard mean at startup?
faqs.a: A brief horn when you turn the key on is the normal system self-test. Any other beep pattern means the engine has flagged a condition. The beep sequence depends on your engine model; your owner's manual lists the codes, or check our alarm codes encyclopedia.

faqs.q: Does the Legend 6-year WOWranty cover every component for six years?
faqs.a: No. It covers most qualifying non-structural components that Legend manufactured or installed when a factory defect causes the failure. The motor, trailer, trolling motor, electronics, batteries, dealer-added accessories, consumables and wear items may follow separate terms.

faqs.q: What does Leakproof for Life cover?
faqs.a: For an eligible all-welded Legend, it covers qualifying leaks through the hull structure caused by defects in factory material or workmanship for as long as the original purchaser owns the boat. Impact, corrosion, misuse, poor trailer support and unauthorized modifications are not factory defects.

faqs.q: Can a Legend hull warranty transfer to a second owner?
faqs.a: Qualifying structural protection may transfer once for up to 10 years from the first owner's original purchase date. Transfer normally requires a timely application, dealer inspection, condition photographs, a fee and Legend approval. Confirm the exact boat and current fee before completing the sale.

faqs.q: Do current Legend pontoons use the 6-year WOWranty?
faqs.a: Current pontoons use a separate 5 | 10 | Lifetime structure. Legend publishes lifetime structural parts with up to 10 years of labour, 10 years on qualifying canvas and upholstery, and 5 years on factory-installed tech, electronics and structural fibreglass.
